To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the La Niña (wet) phase of the ENSO cycle is associated with a suite of processes which threaten terrestrial mammal species in the arid zone of central Australia.

(i) ENSO is a key driver of rainfall variability in arid Australia; (ii) rainfall events associated with the La Nina phase of ENSOs are associated with the loss of native mammals; (iii) the loss of native species was most likely caused by predation; and (iv) predation was most likely caused in turn by a combination of high rainfall, high rodent abundance and the introduction of foxes and cats.
the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSo) has a significant influence on the timing and intensity of processes that threaten terrestrial mammal species in the Australian arid zone.
